title: Make all app notifications configurable (target: toast / in-app / system) via global or extension settings
scope:
# Summary

Make every notification the app sends configurable, via both global settings and per-extension settings, and let the user choose which target(s) each notification is delivered to: toast, in-app, and/or system (OS-level) notification.

# Context

Notifications should not be hard-coded to a single delivery mechanism. Configuration should exist at two levels: global settings (app-wide defaults) and per-extension settings (overrides), with extension settings taking precedence over global. For each notification the user should be able to select any combination of toast, in-app, and system targets. The main work is introducing a shared dispatcher and migrating existing notification call sites to route through it.

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every notification routes through a shared, configurable dispatcher (no notification hard-coded to one mechanism)
- [ ] Global settings let the user set default delivery target(s) for notifications
- [ ] Extension settings can override notification targets per extension
- [ ] The user can choose any combination of toast, in-app, and system targets
- [ ] Precedence is defined and implemented: extension setting overrides global
- [ ] Existing notification call sites are migrated to the dispatcher

# Dev Hints

* Introduce a shared notification abstraction/dispatcher that resolves the effective target(s) from global + extension settings before delivering.
* Toast delivery today goes through `useToastStore` (`src/renderer/stores/toast.store`). "System" = OS-level notifications.
* Align with Constitution Principle VII (error handling): errors must still surface as toasts regardless of configured targets.
